items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Eddie Jefferson put lyrics to 'Yardbird Suite.' ... I was referred to as something like a 'poor man’s Eddie Jefferson' or something like that.

ctx.x: The lyrics, I’m familiar with “Well You Needn’t” but I didn’t know “Yardbird Suite” had lyrics.

That’s very interesting. Because Charlie Parker wrote lyrics to his own song when he was 19 years old, and the song was originally called “What Price Love.” Because he left his first wife to go make music. And he wrote the lyrics. And they’re really good lyrics too. Nobody knew that he was really a lyricist. And then later on Eddie Jefferson put lyrics to “Yardbird Suite.” So I sing ‘em both. I sing Bird’s first, the band blows, and then I go out with — and they’re both kind of historical. I mean you could tell…

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I started to sing the Charlie Parker solo, with lyrics by Eddie Jefferson.

ctx.x: So for those people on YouTube, my name is Monk Rowe and this is Giacomo Gates, and we just saw you perform last night. I took copious notes, so I hope you’ll analyze your own performance with great elan. It occurred to me maybe during the second or third song when you were doing vocalese, how magnificent those solos were that you and the vocalese masters set words to, that one of the ways to appreciate those solos is to listen to them with vocalese, because they are just musical gems.

I agree. I agree. The people that started to do that — Eddie Jefferson, Jon Hendricks, Annie Ross — they had great solos to choose from. People played lyrical stories, melodic lyrical stories. I’m not saying it’s easy to put lyrics to that, but the solos are just amazing. Amazing.
